items.title: Does Nvidia Got This? Interim CEO Colette Kress Says It’s Got This
items.summary: WIRED is tallying up how many times Nvidia’s interim CEO has assured everyone that the company has everything under control.
items.author: Lauren Goode

items.title: Even His Own Officials Don’t Think Trump’s China Trip Will Lead to Progress on AI
items.summary: Fallout from the Nvidia scandal has made any negotiations around AI difficult, officials say.
items.author: Hugo Lowell

items.title: America’s AI Chip War Is Heating Up in the Dumbest Possible Ways
items.summary: The Trump administration announced plans to clamp down on China’s access to AI chips. Apparently, the cheating scandal of the century was the motivation they were missing.
items.author: Louise Matsakis

items.title: Inside Nvidia’s First Post-Jensen All-Hands: Pay Raises and More Equity
items.summary: Interim CEO Colette Kress sought to ease employee concerns following Jensen Huang’s ouster, in part by promising to increase compensation.
items.author: Paresh Dave, Lauren Goode

items.title: Artex Is Criminals’ New Favorite ‘Point-and-Shoot’ AI Hacking Tool
items.summary: Artex and similar penetration testing tools allow newbie hackers to scan targeted systems for vulnerabilities and successfully wage attacks using prompts fed to chatbots.
items.author: Matt Burgess

items.title: ‘Just Ridiculous’: A Famed Philosopher Takes on AI Consciousness
items.summary: Thomas Nagel has done landmark work on consciousness in nonhumans; this week, he won the million-dollar Berggruen Prize for his contributions to the field. And he has a lot of thoughts on AI.
items.author: Steven Levy

items.title: Lovable Wants You to Vibe Code Your Dream Job
items.summary: This Swedish startup dominated the vibe-coded app boom. Two years after launch, Lovable is shifting gears to help users run vibe-coded businesses.
items.author: Reece Rogers

items.title: Over a Third of Gen Z-ers Rely on AI for Friendship
items.summary: Young people who have online-only friends or use AI as a social companion face higher odds of loneliness than those who do not, a new Gallup report reveals.
items.author: Jason Parham
